name: consultation-insights-web
description: Doctor-facing UI for Consultation Insights. Next.js App Router; all backend traffic goes through the server-side BFF in app/api/[...path].
//: Neon Auth is beta-only on npm and auth-ui pins auth to an exact version, so both are pinned exactly rather than with carets.
//dev: `dev` runs HTTPS on purpose. Neon Auth's session-challenge cookie is __Secure- prefixed with the Secure flag, and Safari refuses to store Secure cookies over plain HTTP even on localhost (Chrome and Firefox make an exception). Over http:// the cookie is dropped, so the OAuth callback fails with SESSION_CHALLENGE_COOKIE_NOT_FOUND and you land back on the sign-in screen with no visible error and nothing in the backend logs. The SDK's SessionCookieConfig exposes secret/sessionDataTtl/domain/sameSite only, so the flag cannot be turned off — the origin has to be genuinely secure.
//dev-certs: certificates/*.pem is a self-signed cert generated with openssl, gitignored, and NOT trusted by the system, so the browser warns once per origin. It is used instead of `dev:mkcert` (next dev --experimental-https) because mkcert needs sudo to install a local CA into the system trust store, which cannot be automated. Run `dev:mkcert` yourself once if you would rather have a trusted cert and no warning. `dev:http` is kept for Chrome-only work, and for `gen:api` which does not care.
